ai.s: Moves the Search service's API keys into AWS Secrets Manager with runtime injection into ECS, adds a redacted .env.example and rotates keys.
ai.pr: API keys for the service were held in environment files rather than a managed secrets store.
ai.wy: Security hardening sprint for the Search Anatomy work.
ai.oc: All API keys in AWS Secrets Manager, injected via the ECS task definition secrets block, a redacted .env.example in the repo and all keys rotated after migration.

ai.s: Automates testing, Docker builds and ECS deployment for the Search service through GitHub Actions, blocking broken code from merging.
ai.pr: Tests, image builds and deployments for the service were not fully automated, and nothing stopped broken code from being merged.
ai.wy: Delivery automation sprint for the Search Anatomy work.
ai.oc: Tests on every PR, Docker build and push on merge, auto-deploy to ECS and a branch protection rule.

ai.s: Enforces "Read Only" admin access so restricted users cannot create, edit or delete, including on meeting pages.
ai.pr: Read Only mode did not stop users editing, and user access settings were ignored on Concierge meetings, Meeting program and Speed networking pages.
ai.wy: Access control in the Admin Panel must work as configured.
ai.oc: Read Only mode to block create, edit and delete actions, with access settings respected on the meeting-related pages.

summary: Centralize Visitors logic: single account-level service

ai.s: Centralises Visitors logic into a single account-level service so all Visitors operations go through one API.
ai.pr: Visitors logic and data access were scattered across services and entry points, causing inconsistent behaviour, data risks and complex integrations.
ai.wy: Architecture clean-up to cut maintenance effort and speed up Visitors feature delivery.
ai.oc: A dedicated Visitors service as the single source of truth, key flows migrated, legacy entry points deprecated and integration docs written.

summary: Remove old frontend code and entry points after migration

ai.s: Removes the old Visitors frontend code and routes after the migration, so only the new frontend remains.
ai.pr: The deprecated frontend was still deployed and reachable via legacy routes, confusing developers and adding bundle size and security risk.
ai.wy: Technical debt clean-up following the new Visitors frontend going live.
ai.oc: Old frontend code, assets and exclusive backend dependencies deleted, legacy routes redirected or returning 301/404, and pipelines no longer building it.

summary: WS: merge Messenger and Online rooms + code refactor

ai.s: Merges the Messenger and Online WebSocket rooms into one handler, removing duplicated connection and messaging code.
ai.pr: Two separate WebSocket room implementations duplicated logic and behaved inconsistently, so fixes had to be applied twice.
ai.wy: Architecture clean-up to cut maintenance cost and ease cross-room features.
ai.oc: A single WebSocket implementation with shared base modules and configurable room differences, behaviour preserved and covered by tests.

ai.s: Refactors Visitors email sending into a dedicated service with unified templates, configuration, retries and error handling.
ai.pr: Email logic was scattered and duplicated, so template changes touched many files and delivery errors were handled inconsistently.
ai.wy: Architecture clean-up to make emails easier to change and more reliable.
ai.oc: One email service used across Visitors features, duplicate code removed, behaviour preserved and basic unit tests added.

ai.s: Rebuilds the registration service for resilience, with notification retries, load testing and failure alerts.
ai.pr: Notifications could silently fail and data might not persist under peak load; error spikes and tickets about missing confirmation emails were observed.
ai.wy: Attendees missing confirmations lose trust, and organisers need reliable registration data.
ai.oc: Retries and dead-letter queues for notifications, load testing before peaks and monitoring alerts for registration failures and data loss.

ai.s: Consolidates image upload, validation, resizing, storage and delivery into one service for all Visitors flows.
ai.pr: Image logic was copy-pasted across flows, so resizing and validation varied, avatar sizes differed and the same bugs were fixed in several places.
ai.wy: Architecture clean-up to cut debugging time and improve image loading.
ai.oc: A single image service, Visitors flows migrated to it, scattered legacy code deleted and existing images still working.

ai.s: Adds a V3 POST endpoint to create session tags as first-class entities that sessions can then reference.
ai.pr: In V2, /api/v2/sessions/setTag handled both creating and updating tags and matched by name.
ai.wy: Part of the Public API V3 migration, splitting create and update into clear REST operations.
ai.oc: POST /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/tags creates a tag with name and optional externalId, validated first and returning 201.

ai.s: Adds a V3 PUT endpoint to update an existing session tag by its internal ID.
ai.pr: In V2, tag updates were combined with creation in /api/v2/sessions/setTag, with name-based matching.
ai.wy: Part of the Public API V3 migration, splitting create and update into clear REST operations.
ai.oc: PUT /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/tags/{tagId} supports partial updates of name and externalId, with 404 and 422 handling.

ai.s: Adds a V3 POST endpoint to create session types as first-class entities that sessions can then reference.
ai.pr: In V2, /api/v2/sessions/setType handled both creating and updating types and matched by name.
ai.wy: Part of the Public API V3 migration, splitting create and update into clear REST operations.
ai.oc: POST /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/types creates a type with name and optional externalId, validated first and returning 201.
